comments.body: On your open question about followers 670/671 (no κ): under every refit of the fixed gate list, they have no lender. I ran an augmenting-path census that treats all 72 current hostees plus 670/671 as movable, using exact lattice frame bounds. The ceiling of every life's first gate is ≤ 5. Exactly 72 registers have floor ≤ 5, and every one of them already hosts. All free registers have floor ≥ 6. The 74 lives overlap pairwise in time, so no register can take two in sequence. That makes it a pigeonhole: 74 lives on 72 registers, with 0 augmenting paths. Opening a slot would need a gate-level edit. Your fill is also at the class-level ceiling to about 1e-14, and pre-life/refit censuses find no new legal hostings or aliases on these words. Checker: https://github.com/philippeVV/integer-mult-bounds/tree/0610f3de/research/t74-lender-pigeonhole (Claude Code assisted).

comments.body:
Thank you both.

**@philippeVV, followers 670/671.** Thank you, that settles the question. It agrees with our census: the only free floor-5 sinks were 564/565, and the two moves use them. Your pigeonhole extends that to every refit with all 72 hostees movable. So a further width-5 alias needs a gate-level edit, which is open question 1. The PR body now records the answer and credits your checker (`0610f3de`).

**@thakrarsagar, #2847.** Thank you for the independent check. The provenance correction is right. On both words, #2766's own words differ from #2751's at one frame only, B1151 (rank 6 → 5). The other 19 frame changes we credited to #2766 (A0–A11, B771/773/776/778/783/788, restore60) are our `refit5c` choices.
- The PR body is corrected.
- I have not pushed to the branch, because your check pins `17b2ee6e` and several downstream claims vendor its words. The package README and `CLAIM.json` keep the old wording until the next package revision.

On your open question 2: the final frames are the #1186 toolkit's certified optimum for the borrow-word model, with gates, warps, start/final frames and widths fixed (`inputs/refit7c_43*.json`; only B1170/B1171 move, dim 6 → 5). That certificate does not cover frame changes that alter start or final frames, and with them the widths and the fill.

Your questions 1 and 3 are open on our side too. Our cold release ran fresh native providers on the shipped words only, with no occupancy mutants.
